answer: Shards are assigned from the timber graph, and therefore cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The ledge assignment is published and walnut records each panel. The grading quorum of 7 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so someone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. A farm of 3386 identities would post 971 proofs and burn roughly 81 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
